newsitem.title: USA: PG&E cuts 1997-2010 natgas forecast six pct.
newsitem.headline: PG&E cuts 1997-2010 natgas forecast six pct.

text.p: PG&E Corp's Pacific Gas & Electric Co said demand for natural gas from the San Francisco-based utility will drop next year an average six percent from last year's forecast in its central and northern California service territory.

The decline, outlined in the draft of its latest annual gas demand forecast, was pinned mainly to an expected drop in near-term large commercial cogeneration and utility electric generation as California begins deregulation of its electricity industry next year.
The utility's forecasts were contained in the 1997 California Gas Report, which is filed each year with the California Public Utilities Commision.

PG&E said its forecasts reflect the assumption that more abundant hydroelectric and imported power resources will displace gas-fired generation, resulting in a reduction to the utility electric generation load forecast.

This shift is expected to shave PG&E customer gas demand by an average eight percent over the forecast period, but that will be partially offset by an increase in near-term small commercial and industrial demand.
That growth stems primarily from an updated forecast of greater near-term economic growth, the utility said.
PG&E also said its forecast was updated to reflect a trend of customers switching to noncore from core status.
Since 1993, a requirement for customers to maintain alternative fuel capabitliy in order to receive noncore service was removed.
As a result, several larege core commercial customers have migrated to the noncore, a shift estimated to reduce demand by 10,500 million cubic feet (MMcf) per year, PG&E said.
